solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, answers clash); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A fruit that sounds repulsive

indicators.note: the clue asks for a word that sounds like another word meaning repulsive

parts.note: repulsive means ugly

explanation.surface: A shopper turns up their nose at a fruit whose name sounds off-putting.
explanation.definitionFit: The ugli is a Jamaican citrus fruit, a tangelo with wrinkly yellow-green skin.

clue.text: In France a bull's regularly confined by barriers. As are horses and cows

parts.note: the French word for a is un

indicators.note: the letters picked from the bull are held inside the barriers

parts.note: gates are barriers in fences

indicators.note: taking every other letter of bull's, the second and fourth

explanation.surface: A French bull is penned in by fences, which is just how horses and cows are kept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As are' is a link: the definition reads as a description of horses and cows, the group they belong to.
explanation.definitionFit: Ungulates are hoofed mammals, a group that includes horses and cattle.

clue.text: Imprisoned old fellow must get over sentence just at a critical moment

parts.note: in the nick is British slang for in prison
F is the abbreviation for fellow, as in FRS
time is a prison sentence, as in doing time

explanation.surface: A jailed old man must get over his sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must get over' joins the pieces: in a down clue the earlier pieces sit over TIME. 'The nick' is British slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something happening only just before it would be too late.

clue.text: Woman's letter is inconsiderate

parts.note: Di is a woman's name, and with the possessive gives DI'S
a missive is a letter

explanation.surface: A woman's letter is thoughtless towards its recipient.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who brushes others aside shows no regard for them, treating them as unworthy of attention.

clue.text: Backs justification

definitions.meaning: in football or hockey the backs are the defensive players
a reasoned case argued in support of an action

explanation.surface: Supports a justification.
explanation.definitionFit: A team's backs form its rear guard line, and a reasoned argument for one's conduct is also so called.

clue.text: Your counterparts alone in possession of very right answers at last

indicators.note: the word for alone holds the abbreviation for very within it

parts.note: sole means alone, the only one

indicators.note: takes the final letter of the word answers

explanation.surface: Those who alone hold the very right answers at last are like you.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue addresses you, the reader working the puzzle: your counterparts are others doing the same.
explanation.definitionFit: The reader of a crossword is someone working it out, so people like the reader are those who crack puzzles.

clue.text: Bend in fine line twisting over court

indicators.note: in a down clue the first part sits over the second
the letters of fine plus the abbreviation for line are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A fine line in a tennis court bends as it twists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisting' turns FINE plus L into INFLE; 'over' puts it above CT.
explanation.definitionFit: To inflect is to bend or curve inward, the original sense behind changing a word's form.

clue.text: Processing of English flax plants with 26 is obvious

indicators.note: processing means working raw material over, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the answer to 26 across, a word for times long past

explanation.surface: Processing English flax plants is self-evident, along with something from long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Processing of' rearranges E, FLAX, PLANTS and the answer to 26 across, YORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something needing no explanation is plain and clear on its face.

clue.text: Make a mistake turning up, see Hollywood star as his friends knew him

definitions.text: Hollywood star as his friends knew him

parts.note: to err is to make a mistake

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the word is read upward, backwards

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see or behold

explanation.surface: A fan errs in spotting a film star and calls him by his first name.
explanation.walkthrough: Errol Flynn was the swashbuckling Hollywood star; friends called him by his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Errol was the first name of the actor Flynn, the name his friends used.

clue.text: Pleased grid's well-nigh complete

parts.note: a grate is a grid of bars; the 's is read as is, a link

indicators.note: well-nigh means almost, so the word for complete loses its final letter

parts.note: full means complete

explanation.surface: A setter is delighted that the grid is almost finished.
explanation.definitionFit: Being thankful carries the sense of being glad and satisfied with what one has received.

clue.text: He might knock down mate

definitions.meaning: one who fells trees, a lumberjack
an informal word for a man or chap

explanation.surface: A friend who might floor you.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodsman fells trees, and the colloquial word for a fellow is spelt the same.

clue.text: Former Eastern navy sail

parts.note: late means former, as in the late chairman

explanation.surface: An old Eastern navy's sail.
explanation.definitionFit: A lateen is a triangular sail set on a long yard, used on dhows.

clue.text: Outspoken ego, even around five feet in height

indicators.note: outspoken signals a word said out loud, here the word for ego

parts.note: I is the self, the ego
level means even, flat

explanation.surface: A loud ego, even so, stands about five feet tall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks like a containment signal, but it belongs to the definition, meaning roughly.
explanation.definitionFit: The height of a person's gaze is roughly five feet or so above the ground.

clue.text: Pecuniary source of old currency

indicators.note: the word Pecuniary is the source from which the letters are drawn

explanation.surface: A financial source of old money.
explanation.definitionFit: The ecu was an old French coin and later the European unit of account before the euro.

clue.text: Appropriate footwear for instructors

definitions.meaning: sports shoes, apt for those who train

explanation.surface: Suitable shoes for teachers.
explanation.definitionFit: Sports shoes and coaches share the same word, both tied to training.

clue.text: Refills glass with best drink

parts.note: top means best, as in top marks
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: A host refills a glass with the finest drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Adding more drink to a part-empty glass is the familiar phrasal verb for refilling it.

clue.text: He or she perhaps going to church to pass judgement

parts.note: he and she are examples of pronouns
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A man or woman goes to church to pass judgement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks he or she as examples of a part of speech, not people.
explanation.definitionFit: To pronounce is to declare formally, as a judge pronounces a sentence.

clue.text: He famously wrote short story about return of European king

indicators.note: the shortened story goes about the reversed pair
short means the word for story loses its last letter

parts.note: story taken as written

indicators.note: return means the two letters are read backwards

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for king in chess

explanation.surface: A famous writer produced a short story about a European king's return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts STORY to STOR; 'return of' turns E and K into KE; 'about' puts STOR around it. Bram Stoker wrote Dracula.
explanation.definitionFit: Bram Stoker is the Irish novelist celebrated for Dracula.

clue.text: Foreign character's only half educated

definitions.note: the 's is read as is, linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: only the first half of the word for educated is kept

parts.note: taught means educated

explanation.surface: An outsider is only half schooled.
explanation.definitionFit: Tau is a letter of the Greek alphabet, a character from a foreign script.

clue.text: Once again straighten out tipsy gal in ER

indicators.note: tipsy means drunk and unsteady, so these letters reel into a new order

explanation.surface: A drunk woman in the emergency room needs straightening out again.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is the American emergency room.
explanation.definitionFit: To realign is to bring back into line, setting straight once more.

clue.text: Dance enthusiast joins one comically desperate game

parts.note: a fan is an enthusiast
Desperate Dan is a character in the British comic The Dandy
go is a Japanese board game

explanation.surface: A dance fan joins someone desperate for a game.
explanation.walkthrough: Desperate Dan is the cow-pie-eating strongman of the British children's comic The Dandy.
explanation.definitionFit: The fandango is a lively Spanish dance in triple time.

clue.text: Delivers excellent climbing plant

parts.note: to deliver is to free or set at liberty

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means read upward, backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-class, written AI

explanation.surface: A garden centre delivers a fine climbing plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climbing plant' looks like the definition; 'climbing' turns AI to IA.
explanation.definitionFit: Freesias are fragrant flowering plants grown from corms.

clue.text: Twerps putting name on topless boxes

indicators.note: topless means the word for boxes loses its first letter

parts.note: the box is British slang for television; tellies are TV sets

explanation.surface: Idiots stick names on lidless boxes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxes' means TV sets, British slang 'the box'.
explanation.definitionFit: A nelly is British slang for a silly or feeble person, a fool.

clue.text: Vote to rewrite gaffes, interrupted by Unionist and Republican

indicators.note: the letters of gaffes are written out again in a new order

explanation.surface: A politician votes to amend blunders, interrupted by Unionist and Republican members.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to rewrite' rearranges GAFFES, and 'interrupted by' puts U and R among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Suffrage is the right to vote in elections.

clue.text: Run in to prevent temper tantrum

indicators.note: the abbreviation for run goes in the word for prevent

parts.note: to stop is to prevent
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A dash in to stop a toddler's outburst.
explanation.definitionFit: Strop is British slang for a fit of bad temper, a sulk.

clue.text: House including soldier's hut

indicators.note: the zodiac sign holds the soldier within it

parts.note: Leo is one of the twelve houses of the zodiac
a soldier ant is a kind of ant

explanation.surface: A house that includes a soldier's hut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' means a sign of the zodiac, each of which rules one of the twelve astrological houses; a soldier is a caste of ant.
explanation.definitionFit: A lean-to is a simple shed or hut built against a wall.

clue.text: Antrim inimitably offers famous place on coast

indicators.note: the two words offer up the letters within them

explanation.surface: County Antrim provides an inimitable coastal spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Antrim is a county in Northern Ireland, a misleading lead toward Irish coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Rimini is a well-known Italian resort on the Adriatic coast.

clue.text: Extinct tiger's doom is left strangely unknown in the end

definitions.note: the 's is read as is, a link to the wordplay

indicators.note: places the unknown at the end of the word
strangely means these letters appear oddly rearranged

parts.note: N is an unknown number in algebra

explanation.surface: The doom of an extinct tiger remains strangely unknown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' rearranges DOOM, IS and L to SMILODO.
explanation.definitionFit: Smilodon is the genus of the sabre-toothed cat, an extinct prehistoric predator.

clue.text: Excited spaniel runs energetically at first round new plants

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the abbreviation for new
an excited dog runs around, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of energetically

explanation.surface: An excited spaniel runs energetically around new plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Excited' rearranges SPANIEL, R and E; 'round' puts this around N.
explanation.definitionFit: Perennials are plants that live for more than two years.

clue.text: Finally they go over remembrance for long ago

indicators.note: finally takes the closing letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: In the end they go over memories of times past.
explanation.definitionFit: Days of yore are days long past, an old word for former times.
